'''José María Callejón Bueno''' ({{IPA|es|xoˈse kaʎeˈxon}}; born 11 February 1987) is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] or [[winger (association football)|winger]].

He began his career with the reserve teams of [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], but made a name for himself at [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]]. In 2011 he returned to his previous club and, two years later, left for [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]], where he won two [[Coppa Italia]] tournaments and the [[2014 Supercoppa Italiana]] while appearing in 349 competitive matches (82 goals scored).

An [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21 international]], Callejón made his senior debut for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] in 2014.

==Club career==
===Real Madrid===
A product of [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] youth ranks, Callejón was born in [[Motril]], [[Province of Granada|Granada]], [[Andalusia]]. He made his professional debut for [[Real Madrid Castilla|the reserves]] in May 2007,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1202730486128/noticia/Noticia/Castilla_2-1_Malaga.htm|title=Castilla 2–1 Málaga|publisher=Real Madrid CF|language=es|date=5 May 2007|access-date=21 June 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120219203116/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1202730486128/noticia/Noticia/Castilla_2-1_Malaga.htm|archive-date=19 February 2012}}</ref> and played five games in [[2006–07 Segunda División|that season]]'s [[Segunda División]] without scoring a goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/2013/11/26/real-madrid/305872.html|title=La última plantilla que descendió con el Castilla. ¿Qué fue de ellos?|trans-title=The last squad to be relegated with Castilla. What happened to them?|publisher=Vavel|last=Balderas|first=Miguel Ángel|language=es|date=26 November 2013|access-date=20 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/historico/segunda/plantillas/partidos_jugados.asp?jug=2897&ntemp=2006-07&equ=01&temp=106|title=Player file: Callejón|publisher=[[Liga Nacional de Fútbol Profesional]]|language=es|access-date=21 June 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081010025357/http://www.lfp.es/historico/segunda/plantillas/partidos_jugados.asp?jug=2897&ntemp=2006-07&equ=01&temp=106|archive-date=10 October 2008}}</ref>

In the [[2007–08 Segunda División B|2007–08 campaign]], Callejón appeared in 37 matches and netted 21 times, finishing as team top scorer but in the [[Segunda División B]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2008/04/28/pagina-27/573730/pdf.html|title=El 'pichichi', José Callejón, rescató un punto en el descuento para el filial|trans-title='Pichichi', José Callejón, rescued one point in injury time for the reserves|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|last=Ramírez|first=Fidel|language=es|date=28 April 2008|access-date=14 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1193040472515/1193040943694/jugador/Jugador/Jose_Callejon.htm|title=Stats: José María Callejón Bueno|publisher=Real Madrid CF|language=es|access-date=21 June 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080719111252/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1193040472515/1193040943694/jugador/Jugador/Jose_Callejon.htm|archive-date=19 July 2008}}</ref>

===Espanyol===
[[File:JoseCallejon.JPG|thumb|left|Callejón taking a corner for [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] in 2009]]
At the end of the season, Callejón left Real Madrid (with twin brother [[Juanmi Callejón|Juanmi]]) and signed a four-year contract with [[RCD Espanyol]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202738224852/noticia/ComunicadoOficial/OFFICIAL_ANNOUNCEMENT_2008-06-20.htm|title=Real Madrid and Espanyol reach an agreement for the transfer of Castilla's José Callejón|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=20 June 2008|access-date=20 June 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080626095726/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202738224852/noticia/ComunicadoOficial/OFFICIAL_ANNOUNCEMENT_2008-06-20.htm|archive-date=26 June 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://football.uk.reuters.com/european/news/455DB3FA-3D1A-11DD-BC18-D90C8CD11FD2.php?rpc=401&&refresh=true|title=Espanyol sign Real Madrid B striker Callejón|agency=[[Reuters]]|date=18 June 2008|access-date=18 June 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121211215508/http://football.uk.reuters.com/european/news/455DB3FA-3D1A-11DD-BC18-D90C8CD11FD2.php?rpc=401&&refresh=true|archive-date=11 December 2012}}</ref> He made his [[La Liga]] debut on 20 September 2008, as a late [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in a 1–1 home draw against [[Getafe CF]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elconfidencial.com/deportes/futbol/liga/2008-09-20/el-espanyol-reacciona-a-tiempo-para-guardar-el-liderato_357856/|title=El Espanyol reacciona a tiempo para guardar el liderato|trans-title=Espanyol react on time to retain first place|newspaper=[[El Confidencial]]|language=es|date=20 September 2008|access-date=3 May 2018}}</ref>

On 15 March 2009, as Espanyol struggled immensely in the league – eventually [[2008–09 La Liga|ranking in tenth position]] – Callejón scored his first goal for the [[Catalonia|Catalans]] in a 3–3 home draw to [[RCD Mallorca]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.publico.es/actualidad/espanyol-mas-epico-temporada-queda.html|title=3–3. El Espanyol más épico de la temporada se queda sin premio ante el Mallorca|trans-title=3–3. Most epic Espanyol of season do not have prize against Mallorca|newspaper=[[Público (Spain)|Público]]|language=es|date=15 March 2009|access-date=3 May 2018}}</ref> He continued to be an undisputed starter under [[Mauricio Pochettino]] the following campaigns, operating mainly as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/espanyol/callejon-el-gol-me-deja-mas-tranquilo-837506|title=Callejón: "El gol me deja más tranquilo"|trans-title=Callejón: "Goal makes me more at ease"|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|language=es|date=15 February 2010|access-date=3 May 2018}}</ref>

On 15 January 2011, Callejón scored twice to help to a 2–1 away defeat of [[Sevilla FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=301902&cc=5739|title=Callejon nets brace|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=15 January 2011|access-date=1 March 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628234705/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=301902&cc=5739|archive-date=28 June 2011}}</ref> He only missed one league game and netted six times for the ''Pericos'', who [[2010–11 La Liga|finished comfortably in mid-table]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20110904/rcd-espanyol/el-espanyol-cambia-dinero-por-goles_54211855294.html|title=El Espanyol cambia dinero por goles|trans-title=Espanyol trade money for goals|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|language=es|date=4 September 2011|access-date=3 May 2018}}</ref>

===Return to Real Madrid===
On 23 May 2011, Callejón re-joined Real Madrid on a five-year deal effective as of 1 July, for a reported fee of [[Euro|€]]5.5 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330059096711/noticia/ComunicadoOficial/Official_announcement:_Jose_Callejon_to_play_for_Real_Madrid.htm|title=Jose Callejon to play for Real Madrid|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=23 May 2011|access-date=23 May 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110526190753/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330059096711/noticia/ComunicadoOficial/Official_announcement%3A_Jose_Callejon_to_play_for_Real_Madrid.htm|archive-date=26 May 2011}}</ref> On 16 July, he played his first match for them in a 4–1 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] victory over the [[Los Angeles Galaxy]], scoring the first goal of the game in the 30th minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlssoccer.com/matchcenter/2011-07-16-la-galaxy-vs-real-madrid/stats|title=LA Galaxy 1–4 Real Madrid|publisher=[[Major League Soccer]]|date=16 July 2011|access-date=17 July 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720234459/http://www.mlssoccer.com/matchcenter/2011-07-16-la-galaxy-vs-real-madrid/stats|archive-date=20 July 2011}}</ref>

On 2 October 2011, Callejón netted his first official goal for Real Madrid after coming on midway through the second half of an away fixture against former club Espanyol; he scored from a [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] [[Assist (association football)|assist]] in an eventual 4–0 win but did not celebrate the goal, instead raising his arms in the air in a mark of respect for his former employer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323973?cc=5739|title=Higuain gives Mourinho plenty to ponder|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=2 October 2011|access-date=2 October 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111005152304/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323973?cc=5739|archive-date=5 October 2011}}</ref>

Profiting from the fact that his team had already qualified from the [[UEFA Champions League]] [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League|group stage]] as leaders, Callejón was handed a rare start by manager [[José Mourinho]] on 22 November 2011, and responded by scoring a brace in a 6–2 home rout of [[NK Dinamo Zagreb]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01f7-0e79a8b7cb4f-0598f140488b-1000--perfect-madrid-put-six-past-dinamo/|title=Perfect Madrid put six past Dinamo|publisher=UEFA|last=Bryan|first=Paul|date=22 November 2011|access-date=22 November 2011}}</ref> He added another two in the last round, at [[AFC Ajax]] (3–0).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01f8-0e7c69a4490a-e01621d81b08-1000--ajax-shattered-as-madrid-complete-perfect-set/|title=Ajax shattered as Madrid complete perfect set|publisher=UEFA|last=Brookman|first=Derek|date=7 December 2011|access-date=7 December 2011}}</ref>

As a starter, Callejón continued with his impressive scoring form: he scored once in a 6–2 away win over Sevilla on 17 December 2011,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323882?cc=5739|title=Real rout Sevilla|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=17 December 2011|access-date=21 December 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120722220859/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323882?cc=5739|archive-date=22 July 2012}}</ref> and in the tie against [[SD Ponferradina]] for [[2011–12 Copa del Rey|the season]]'s [[Copa del Rey]] he netted three of his team's seven aggregate goals, one away and two at home.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2011_12/copa/dieciseisavos/ida/pnf_rma/|title=Un chupito revitalizante|trans-title=Invigorating shot|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|last=Friede|first=Sergio|language=es|date=13 December 2011|access-date=21 December 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2011_12/copa/dieciseisavos/vuelta/rma_pnf/|title=El Madrid ficha hacia octavos|trans-title=Madrid sign last-16|newspaper=Marca|last=Friede|first=Sergio|language=es|date=20 December 2011|access-date=21 December 2011}}</ref>

On 14 January 2012, Callejón scored the winner in a 2–1 defeat of Mallorca, helping the visitors come from behind with his 84th-minute long-range strike.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=323865&cc=5739|title=Real survive scare to go clear|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=14 January 2012|access-date=20 January 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120714174831/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=323865&cc=5739|archive-date=14 July 2012}}</ref> He added another the following matchday, closing the score in a 4–1 home victory against [[Athletic Bilbao]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/324021?cc=5739|title=Real Madrid spot on|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=22 January 2012|access-date=24 January 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120128042352/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/324021?cc=5739|archive-date=28 January 2012}}</ref>

===Napoli===
[[File:Barça - Napoli - 20140806 - Salut des équipes.jpg|thumb|right|Callejón ''(wearing No.7)'' playing for [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], 2014]]
On 9 July 2013, Italian club [[SSC Napoli]] announced that they had reached an agreement for the transfer of Callejón for €10 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/2892/transfer-zone/2013/07/09/4105916/real-madrid-attacker-callejon-set-to-join-napoli?ICID=OP|title=Real Madrid attacker Callejon set to join Napoli|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|last=Kvesa|first=Chris|date=9 July 2013|access-date=10 July 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sscnapoli.it/static/news/Callejon-e-a-Napoli-538.aspx|title=Callejon è a Napoli|trans-title=Callejon is in Naples|publisher=S.S.C Napoli|language=it|date=10 July 2013|access-date=10 July 2013}}</ref> The four-year deal was confirmed two days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2013/07/11/4110630/napoli-snap-up-callejon?ICID=AR_RS_1|title=Napoli snap up Callejon|publisher=Goal|last=Fenn|first=Alec|date=11 July 2013|access-date=13 July 2013}}</ref>

Callejón scored in his [[Serie A]] debut on 25 August, netting the opener in a 3–0 home win over [[Bologna FC 1909]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Squadre/Napoli/25-08-2013/napoli-bologna-diretta-campionato-calcio-seriea-prima-giornata-201031849154.shtml|title=Napoli-Bologna 3–0: apre Callejon, poi la doppietta di super Hamsik|trans-title=Napoli-Bologna 3–0: Callejon starts it, then double by super Hamsik|newspaper=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]|last=Bozza|first=Gennaro|language=it|date=25 August 2013|access-date=11 December 2013}}</ref> and went on to find the net a further seven times in his first 20 official appearances. On 22 October, he scored his first goal in [[UEFA competitions|Europe]] for his new team, grabbing his team's first in a 2–1 victory at [[Olympique de Marseille]] in the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|Champions League group stage]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0ea8c66f9c1e-80f5a63c69ae-1000--napoli-make-their-mark-in-marseille/|title=Napoli make their mark in Marseille|publisher=UEFA|last=Burke|first=Chris|date=22 October 2013|access-date=27 October 2014}}</ref>

On 3 May 2014, Callejón set up [[Dries Mertens]] for the third goal in a 3–1 win against [[ACF Fiorentina]] in [[2014 Coppa Italia final|the final]] of the [[Coppa Italia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27271913|title=Coppa Italia final: Rafael Benitez's Napoli beat Fiorentina 3–1|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=3 May 2014|access-date=13 May 2014}}</ref> He scored once in the final game of [[2013–14 Serie A|the season]], a 5–1 home rout of [[Hellas Verona FC]] on 18 May; his strike after five minutes was Napoli's 100th goal in all competitions that season, and his 20th overall.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/299494/report|title=Five-star finish for Napoli|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=18 May 2014|access-date=19 May 2014}}</ref>

Callejón netted his first goal of [[2014–15 SSC Napoli season|2014–15]] on the opening day of [[2014–15 Serie A|the campaign]], the opener in a 2–1 win over [[Genoa CFC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/italian-serie-a/match/403834/genoa-napoli/report|title=Genoa 1–2 Napoli|publisher=ESPN FC|date=31 August 2014|access-date=19 October 2014}}</ref> His second came on 24 September, as he scored at the stroke of half-time to put his side up 3–2 against [[Palermo FC|US Città di Palermo]] in an eventual 3–3 home draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/italian-serie-a/match/403803/napoli-palermo/report|title=Napoli 3–3 Palermo|publisher=ESPN FC|date=24 September 2014|access-date=19 October 2014}}</ref> On 19 October, he scored twice in a 2–2 draw at [[Inter Milan]], with all four of the game's goals coming in the last 11 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/italian-serie-a/match/403774/internazionale-napoli/report|title=Hernanes header helps Inter Milan to a 2–2 draw with Napoli|publisher=ESPN FC|date=19 October 2014|access-date=19 October 2014}}</ref>

In the [[Derby del Sole]] match against [[AS Roma]] on 2 November 2014, Callejón hit the post and had a shot saved off the line before eventually finding the net late on in the 2–0 victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/nov/03/higuain-napoli-roma-match-of-fear|title=Gonzalo Higuaín keeps rolling for Napoli in 'match of fear' against Roma|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|last=Bandini|first=Nicky|date=3 November 2014|access-date=4 November 2014}}</ref> The strike took his league goal tally to eight on the season, two more than his closest competitors, and he was included in the Serie A Team of the Week lineup.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://forzaitalianfootball.com/2014/11/serie-a-2014-15-team-of-the-week-round-10/|title=Serie A 2014–15: Team Of The Week – Round 10|publisher=Forza Italian Football|date=3 November 2014|access-date=4 November 2014}}</ref>

On 17 September 2015, Callejón scored twice in Napoli's first game of the [[UEFA Europa League]] group stage, a [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League|5–0 home rout]] of [[Club Brugge KV]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0225-0e91c0b3e019-c42fe133e967-1000--sparkly-napoli-flatten-club-brugge/|title=Sparkly Napoli flatten Club Brugge|publisher=UEFA|date=17 September 2015|access-date=23 October 2015}}</ref> For the same competition, away to [[FC Midtjylland]] on 22 October, he volleyed a long pass from [[Kalidou Koulibaly]] to open a 4–1 victory; [[UEFA]] dubbed the latter effort an "early contender for goal of the group stage".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0226-0e9240f2e7ad-a00af6073d34-1000--sparkling-napoli-finishes-flatten-midtjylland/|title=Sparkling Napoli finishes flatten Midtjylland|publisher=UEFA|date=22 October 2015|access-date=23 October 2015}}</ref>

Callejón marked his 200th appearance for the ''Azzurri'' with his 57th goal on 9 April 2017, in a 3–0 league win against [[SS Lazio]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/100947/serie-week-31-did-you-know|title=Serie A Week 31: Did You Know?|publisher=Football Italia|last=Campanale|first=Susan|date=10 April 2017|access-date=20 April 2017}}</ref> His 300th came on 28 April 2019, in the 2–0 away victory over [[Frosinone Calcio]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/137440/napoli-fans-reject-callejon-shirt|title=Napoli fans reject Callejon shirt|publisher=Football Italia|last=Campanale|first=Susy|date=28 April 2019|access-date=28 April 2019}}</ref>

In August 2020, the 33-year-old Callejón left the [[Stadio San Paolo]] after his contract expired.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://football-italia.net/napoli-bid-farewell-to-callejon/|title=Napoli bid farewell to Callejon|publisher=Football Italia|last=Campanale|first=Susy|date=9 August 2020|access-date=2 June 2023}}</ref>

===Fiorentina===
On 5 October 2020, Callejón agreed to a deal with Fiorentina.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.acffiorentina.com/en/news/all/news-men-first-team/2020-10-05/callejon-completes-fiorentina-move|title=Callejon completes Fiorentina move|publisher=ACF Fiorentina|date=5 October 2020|access-date=6 November 2020|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201106163113/https://www.acffiorentina.com/en/news/all/news-men-first-team/2020-10-05/callejon-completes-fiorentina-move|archive-date=6 November 2020}}</ref> He scored twice in competitive matches during his spell, once in [[2021–22 Serie A|the league]] against [[UC Sampdoria]] (3–1 home win)<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/fiorentina/2021/11/30/news/fiorentina-sampdoria_3-1_callejon_vlahovic_e_sottil_ribaltano_i_blucerchiati-328446075/|title=Fiorentina-Sampdoria 3–1: Callejon, Vlahovic e Sottil ribaltano i blucerchiati|trans-title=Fiorentina-Sampdoria 3–1: Callejon, Vlahovic and Sottil take blue-circled down|newspaper=[[La Repubblica]]|last=Luchini|first=Giacomo|language=it|date=30 November 2021|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> and once in the [[2020–21 Coppa Italia|domestic cup]] to help beat [[Calcio Padova]] 2–1 also at home.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/sport/calcio/2020/10/28/calcio-coppa-italia-fiorentina-padova-2-1_321aabc7-c35b-497a-bc1f-962dcded61e0.html|title=Calcio: Coppa Italia; Fiorentina-Padova 2–1|trans-title=Football: Italian Cup; Fiorentina-Padova 2–1|publisher=[[Agenzia Nazionale Stampa Associata]]|language=it|date=28 October 2020|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref>

===Granada===
Callejón returned to Spain on 25 July 2022 after nine years away, signing a one-year contract with [[Granada CF]] with the option of an extension based on sporting performance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.granadacf.es/noticia/comunicado-oficial-jose-callejon-nuevo-jugador-del-granada-cf|title=Comunicado oficial {{!}} José Callejón, nuevo jugador del Granada CF|trans-title=Official statement {{!}} José Callejón, new Granada CF player|publisher=Granada CF|language=es|date=25 July 2022|access-date=25 July 2022}}</ref> He won the second tier in his [[2022–23 Segunda División|first season]], appearing in all 42 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.granadaenjuego.com/Granada-CF/callejon--el-hijo-prodigo-que-ha-cumplido-la-mision-|title=Callejón, el hijo pródigo que ha cumplido la misión|trans-title=Callejón, the prodigal son who got job done|publisher=Granada en Juego|last=Azcoytia|first=Jorge|language=es|date=5 July 2023|access-date=5 September 2023}}</ref>

===Later career===
In July 2024, aged 37, Callejón joined [[Primera Federación]] club [[Marbella FC]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2024/07/24/jose-callejon-ficha-por-el-marbella/|title=José Callejón ficha por el Marbella|trans-title=José Callejón signs for Marbella|newspaper=[[Infobae]]|language=es|date=23 July 2024|access-date=25 July 2024}}</ref> On 24 August, he scored the only goal as the hosts beat his former employers Castilla.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/mas_futbol/el-castilla-se-estrella-contra-el-marbella-de-callejon-n/|title=El Castilla se estrella contra el Marbella de Callejón|trans-title=Castilla crash against Callejón's Marbella|newspaper=Diario AS|last=Cariño|first=Carlos|language=es|date=24 August 2024|access-date=5 May 2025}}</ref>

On 19 May 2025, Callejón announced that he would retire at the end of [[2024–25 Primera Federación|the season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://marbellafc.es/nos-jugamos-la-vida-y-honramos-la-historia-callejon-se-retira/|title=Nos jugamos la vida y honramos la historia… ¡¡Callejón se retira!!|trans-title=We are playing for our lives and we have honoured the history… Callejón retires!!|publisher=Marbella FC|language=es|date=19 May 2025|access-date=28 May 2025}}</ref> Five days later, in his last appearance, he opened an eventual 2–0 home win over [[Antequera CF]], with his team avoiding relegation with that result.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/primera-rfef/2025/05/25/jose-callejon-retira-final-pelicula.html|title=José Callejón se retira con un final de película|trans-title=José Callejón retires with movie-like ending|newspaper=Marca|last=Fernández R.|first=Juanje|language=es|date=25 May 2025|access-date=28 May 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Callejón made his debut for the [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain under-21 team]] on 25 March 2008 against [[Kazakhstan national under-21 football team|Kazakhstan]] in a [[2009 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] [[2009 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification|qualifier]]; he entered the field in the 46th minute after replacing [[Bojan Krkić]], and scored shortly after in a 5–0 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/under21/fixturesresults/round=15084/match=300312/report=ev.html|title=Spain 5–0 Kazakhstan|publisher=UEFA|date=25 March 2008|access-date=20 June 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080520104210/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/under21/fixturesresults/round%3D15084/match%3D300312/report%3Dev.html|archive-date=20 May 2008}}</ref>

On 7 November 2014, Callejón was called up to [[Spain national football team|the full side]] for the first time, being picked by [[Vicente del Bosque]] for matches against [[Belarus national football team|Belarus]] and [[Germany national football team|Germany]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sefutbol.com/en/official-23-man-squad-matches-against-belarus-and-germany|title=Official: 23-man squad for the matches against Belarus and Germany|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]|date=7 November 2014|access-date=7 November 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141107173850/http://www.sefutbol.com/en/official-23-man-squad-matches-against-belarus-and-germany|archive-date=7 November 2014}}</ref> He made his debut on the 15th against the former, coming on for [[Santi Cazorla]] in the 69th minute of the 3–0 triumph in [[Huelva]] for the [[UEFA Euro 2016]] [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying|qualifying phase]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/0253-0d7f8d20415a-6e68168eeaec-1000--much-changed-spain-dominate-belarus/|title=Much-changed Spain dominate Belarus|publisher=UEFA|last=Hunter|first=Graham|date=15 November 2014|access-date=15 November 2014}}</ref>

==Style of play==
A versatile, tenacious and hard-working right-footed player, Callejón was capable of playing anywhere along the front line, and was used as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] or a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] on either flank, in the centre as an [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]] and as a [[Forward (association football)#Second striker|supporting striker]]. Although he usually occupied a position in or behind the main attacking line, due to his personality and ability to provide balance to his teams by linking-up play between the forwards and midfielders, he was also capable of playing in the [[Forward (association football)#Centre-forward|centre]] as a [[Forward (association football)#Striker|main striker]], and was also occasionally deployed in deeper roles under Mourinho during his time at Real Madrid, as a [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|central midfielder]] or even as an attacking [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|full-back]] or [[Defender (association football)#Wing-back|wing-back]].

Speed, creativity and technical ability enabled Callejón to both create and score goals. He would characteristically lose his markers with attacking runs in behind the defensive line and into the area from deeper or wider areas, and head the ball in spite of his average stature.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/calcio/calcio_mercato/2013/07/01-326885/Napoli,+ecco+Callejon%3A+il+pupillo+di+Mourinho|title=Napoli, ecco Callejon: il pupillo di ==Personal life==
Callejón's twin brother [[Juanmi Callejón|Juanmi]] was also a footballer, and both were Real Madrid graduates.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2007/12/06/mas_futbol/1196926019_850215.html|title=José y Juanmi Callejón, dos gemelos y diez goles|trans-title=José and Juanmi Callejón, two twins and ten goals|newspaper=Diario AS|last=Catalán|first=José Vicente|language=es|date=6 December 2007|access-date=13 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.joinfutbol.com/es/los_gemelos_callejon_hermanos_pero_rivales_en_el_terreno_de_juego_16666.php|title=Los gemelos Callejón, hermanos pero rivales en el terreno de juego|trans-title=Callejón twins, brothers but rivals on the pitch|publisher=Join Futbol|language=es|date=22 October 2008|access-date=10 July 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131128111732/http://www.joinfutbol.com/es/los_gemelos_callejon_hermanos_pero_rivales_en_el_terreno_de_juego_16666.php|archive-date=28 November 2013}}</ref>

On 6 November 2020, he tested positive for [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.acffiorentina.com/en/news/all/news-men-first-team/2020-11-06/medical-report-callejon|title=Medical report: Callejon|publisher=ACF Fiorentina|date=6 November 2020|access-date=6 November 2020|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201106164102/https://www.acffiorentina.com/en/news/all/news-men-first-team/2020-11-06/medical-report-callejon|archive-date=6 November 2020}}</ref>
